evidence: Run-D.M.C.'s 'Peter Piper' (from 'Raising Hell', 1986) samples the bell pattern and drum break from Bob James's 'Take Me to the Mardi Gras' (1975), credited on sample-database entries and widely discussed by both artists; Run-D.M.C. referred to the bells in the beat as 'Hell's Bells.'

earlier.title: Take Me to the Mardi Gras

trackPair.whatToListenFor: James's original is a laid-back jazz-funk instrumental with a chiming bell pattern buried in the arrangement. Run-D.M.C. pulls just the bells and the break to the front, loops them, and raps directly over the loop, with nothing else in the mix competing with it.

explanation: 'Take Me to the Mardi Gras' (1975) by the jazz musician Bob James has a distinctive bell sound that Run-D.M.C. looped for 'Peter Piper' (1986). Producers nicknamed the loop 'Hell's Bells', and it went on to appear in dozens of other hip-hop records. It is one of the clearest single-source sample lines on this map: one 1975 jazz-funk recording, one 1986 rap record, widely acknowledged and disputed by nobody.
